comment: HD graphics (docs/HD-GRAPHICS.md): the source of the art in data/native/hd (made by make hd-art, not in the repository), Peter Johnson's runtime art pack (assets/atlas-hd) as built from OpenCiv2's repository of assets openciv2/openciv2-assets (repo; its assets/music, sound, heralds and wonders are OpenCiv2's own media, data/own-assets.json) at this commit (sha), so that what is merged there is used without waiting for a release. tools/build_hd_pack.py fetches the commit's files the pack is built from (its runtime-inputs.json's, its builder's and notices: a partial clone in ~/.cache/openciv2, git checking each against its id), builds the pack with its tools/build_atlas.py (as its release does, in a container with the pinned Pillow) and makes data/native/hd from that data/atlas-hd.pack: the pictures the game draws, whose keys begin with one of keep and with none of drop (those src/platform/hd.c and src/game/hd_graphics.cpp draw: crops of the sheets and of the libraries' pictures, their tints, the terrain's blends, fog, the whole sheets, the resource pictures hd.c paints whole (its WHOLE), the throne room's pieces and empty hall, the advances' icons, the spaceship's pieces; dropped: the throne room's decorations, the crops hd.c does not draw (its NOT_CROPPED_KEYS), the city view's houses but the industrial era's rows), at most as large as drawn; and those whose keys begin with one of synth, which src/platform/synth.c reads to make the original's pictures where the game folder lacks them (docs/NO-INSTALL.md: the sheets and their crops, the libraries' GIF resources and their crops, civ2.exe's bitmaps, cursors and icons), at the original's size where the game does not draw them; but never those whose keys begin with one of exclude: the pack's leaders' portraits whole (mk.dll 220 to 261: the game takes only their crops) and the sheets of small faces (210, 211), and the portraits' crops no tribe is given (src/game/hd_graphics.cpp's hd_portraits: the pack's 42 are people of its own, not the tribes' leaders, so each tribe is given the one that fits it where OpenCiv2's historical portrait of its own leader, data/native/portraits (data/own-assets.json), is missing; synth.c makes those pictures dark frames). A picture of another kind drawn or read there is to be added here. Upgrading the art: sha here (git ls-remote REPO main), then the tool.
